title: Niamh
description: A ray tracing curriculum with three renderers that draw the same Cornell box, each one better than the last.
about: Code for a multi-part article on physically based rendering. rtsimple is an interactive Whitted tracer in browser JavaScript. rtadvanced is a C++20 path tracer covering MIS, spectral rendering, bidirectional path tracing, Metropolis light transport, photon mapping, participating media, subsurface scattering and a feature-guided denoiser. rtoptimized is a wavefront path tracer in WebGPU, fed by rtadvanced's scene loader and BVH compiled to WebAssembly, with a real-time ReSTIR mode and native CUDA and Vulkan ports.

title: Nemeton
description: An offline-first festival schedule that installs on phones as a PWA and receives live schedule changes from organizers.
about: A prototype built with Cascadian Midsummer 2026 data, for festivals where the venue network fails. It's an npm workspaces monorepo: a Vite + React web app that keeps the lineup and itineraries in IndexedDB through Dexie, with a custom Workbox service worker; a Hono server on Node's built-in SQLite that pushes change batches over Server-Sent Events; and an organizer CLI. The CLI previews every delay, move or cancellation before publishing, CSV imports publish only the differences, and the server refuses a change if someone else published first.

title: Ogma
description: A desktop Markdown editor for writing, vocabulary and linguistic research, with per-section notes and AI drafting.
about: An Electron + React + TypeScript app built on CodeMirror. It shows a document as output, notes, or both, using notes blocks under each heading. A Python FastAPI sidecar, launched by the app with a per-launch token, routes AI tasks across Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, OpenAI-compatible hosts and a local 4-bit Qwen model on CUDA. AI drafts and agent edits arrive as accept/reject suggestions rather than being written straight to the file. It also has an offline Wiktionary dictionary, full-text search, version history, and atomic saves that keep the file's encoding.

title: Portland Tree Data
description: A map and charts of Portland, Oregon's street trees, built from a Python data-prep pipeline.
about: A Python script fetches Portland's public tree GeoJSON, normalizes it and computes summary metrics, writing the GeoJSON and a summary for the frontend. The frontend is a Vite + React app with an interactive Leaflet map, filters and Recharts charts.

title: Deasil
description: The site behind deasil.org: writing, photography and small browser programs, on a Sanity CMS synced from SmugMug and Notion.
about:
The front end is a Next.js 15 / React 19 site with MUI that reads articles and photographs from Sanity. Its programs section has Sundial (sun, moon and wheel-of-the-year clocks on Leaflet maps), Aria (a generative music tracker with instruments built as node graphs, whose Web Audio engine can render a song to WAV faster than real time), Altar (tarot spreads), Glyph (runes and ancient scripts) and Voluspa (comparing translations stanza by stanza).

The backend is a Sanity studio with schemas for photographs with EXIF metadata, albums, nested folders, posts, authors and categories. Custom studio plugins mirror the SmugMug gallery tree over OAuth 1.0a and import posts from a Notion database.

title: Kybos
description: An interactive visualizer for hypercubes, 4D polytopes and hyperspheres in 2 to 8 dimensions.
about: Rotate a hypercube, 24-cell, 600-cell or hypersphere in any of its planes and watch its projection into 3D change. Hyperspheres are drawn through stereographic projection, and the view state lives in the URL so any orientation can be shared.

title: Kosmos
description: Sorting, searching and graph algorithms you can watch, scrub through and hear.
about:
Each algorithm runs once against a recorder that logs every comparison, swap, write and visit along with what it replaced, so the trace plays forwards and backwards: play, step, scrub or rewind at any speed. Every operation is coloured and becomes a short tone whose pitch follows the value it touched and whose position sets the stereo pan.

There are 31 sorts (quicksort variants, Timsort, introsort, radix, bitonic and odd–even merge networks, and a few jokes) with six drawing styles and a four-lane race, 8 array searches with a probe-count comparison, 6 string matchers including KMP, Boyer–Moore and Z, 9 maze generators and 7 pathfinders on an editable grid with weighted terrain, and 10 algorithms on a random planar graph: Dijkstra, A*, Bellman–Ford, Prim, Kruskal, Borůvka, colouring and topological sort.

title: Apax
description: A pixel drawing app built around rotational and reflectional symmetries.

title: Seed of Life
description: Sacred-geometry circle patterns, from the Vesica Piscis and Seed of Life out to the Flower of Life, exportable as SVG, PNG or JPG.
about: Every pattern is made of circles of one radius. In ring layout the circles sit evenly spaced around a ring (the original pen). In lattice layout they sit on a hexagonal lattice that grows outward one generation at a time: generation 1 is the Seed of Life and generation 2 is the Flower of Life. 'Complete petals' draws one more generation and clips it to the boundary circle with an SVG clipPath, which gives the traditional Flower of Life. The SVG on screen is the file you download; PNG and JPG are drawn onto a canvas at twice the size.
features: Presets: Vesica Piscis, Seed of Life, Egg of Life, Flower of Life
Ring layout or hex-lattice layout grown by generations, with adjustable spacing
Boundary circle and clipped 'complete petals' for the classic Flower of Life
Translucent fills with blend modes (multiply, screen, difference)
Slow spin animation at an adjustable speed and direction
Download as SVG, or as PNG/JPG at 2x

title: Aria
description: Write melodies as scale degrees and hear them in any key, scale or mode, with a live piano roll and shareable links.
about: Melodies are written as scale degrees (0 is the root, 1 the next note up, -1 the next note down), so the same numbers work in any key and in any of 18 scales and modes. Each scale is a list of semitone steps; a degree's pitch is the root plus the sum of steps, and its frequency is 16.352 Hz × 2^(n/12). Playback runs on the Tone.js Transport (the Web Audio clock), and Tone.Draw lights each note in the piano roll at the moment it sounds.
features: Piano roll with in-scale rows shaded and the playing note highlighted in sync
Tempo (BPM) and note-length controls that change live while playing
Sine, triangle, square or sawtooth waveform
Random melody generator with a clickable history of past melodies
Settings saved in the URL hash, with a copy-link button

title: Simone
description: A musical memory game: repeat a growing, speeding-up sequence of notes on a 4, 9 or 16 button board.
about: Each button is one note of a randomly chosen scale and one hue of an evenly spaced rainbow, so a sequence can be remembered by sight or by ear. Simone plays a sequence, you repeat it, and each success adds a note and makes playback a little faster. The sequence, your position and the game phase live in refs so timer callbacks and key handlers always see current values.
features: 2×2, 3×3 or 4×4 boards
Keyboard play on the left of a QWERTY keyboard (QWE/ASD/ZXC and similar), with keys shown on the buttons
Playback speeds up with each level
Strict mode (a mistake ends the game) or forgiving mode (the sequence replays)
Best level saved per board size and mode
Game-over buzz that marks the wrong button and shows the right one

title: N-Body Gravity Simulator
description: Gravity sandbox: pick a preset, fling in new bodies and watch orbits form, with a live readout of how well energy is conserved.
about: Every body pulls on every other with Newton's law, softened at short range so close passes don't blow up. Motion is stepped with a fixed-step leapfrog (kick-drift-kick) integrator, which keeps energy error bounded instead of drifting the way simple Euler stepping does. Presets range from the original spinning ring to a binary star with planets and the three-body figure-eight orbit.
features: Presets: ring galaxy, binary star with circling planets, collapsing random cloud, figure-eight three-body orbit
Click to drop a body, drag to launch it
Sliders for G, softening, timescale and body count
Pause, single-step and fading trails
Live total energy and drift readout

title: Merging Balls
description: Hundreds of balls bounce under gravity and merge on contact, conserving area and momentum, until only a few giants remain.
about: Balls bounce around a box under gravity; when two touch they merge into one, keeping total area and momentum (the merged ball moves at the mass-weighted average velocity). A grid of cells finds touching pairs: each ball is compared only with balls in nearby cells, not with every other ball. Color shows how much mass each ball has absorbed.
features: Press and hold to spray in new balls
Sliders for starting count, gravity and bounce
Color by size, on a log scale from cyan to red
Live stats: balls left, largest radius, merge count
Grid-based collision search instead of checking every pair

title: Decoding Text
description: Scrambled glyphs resolve into your text one random character at a time, with adjustable speed and a choice of glyph sets.
about: Each tick, every unresolved character either locks to its true value with a fixed probability or flips to a new random glyph. Each character's wait is random, so a few lock almost at once and a long tail holds out; anything left after twice the average is forced into place. In cycle mode, phrases separated by blank lines are decoded one after another.
features: Glyph sets: letters, binary, hex, katakana, box-drawing symbols
Speed and settle-time sliders that adjust the running animation
Multi-line input with Ctrl+Enter to decode
Cycle mode that decodes a list of phrases in turn
Keep-spaces toggle; unresolved characters shown dimmed

title: Hacker Typer
description: Mash the keyboard to "write" famous source code: Research Unix, Apollo 11, Linux 0.01, DOOM or Quake III.
about: Every keypress reveals the next few characters of a real historic source file fetched from GitHub. The only state that changes while you type is the length of the visible prefix; the highlighted HTML is derived from it with useMemo. Alt three times flashes ACCESS GRANTED and Caps Lock three times flashes ACCESS DENIED, as in the classic hacker typer.
features: Five historic files: Research Unix C compiler, Apollo 11 ignition routine, Linux 0.01 boot sector, DOOM renderer, Quake III math library
Syntax highlighting for C and x86 assembly, plus a small custom grammar for Apollo Guidance Computer assembly
Characters-per-key slider
Progress bar with a line counter
ACCESS GRANTED / DENIED overlay on key combos, with on-screen buttons too
Tap to type on touch screens

title: Numeric Base Converter
description: Type a number of any length in any base from 1 to 36 and watch every other base update, with a place-value breakdown.
about: All the math uses BigInt, so numbers of any length convert exactly. Parsing uses Horner's rule (value = value x B + digit) so a bad digit can be named precisely. Printing uses BigInt's toString(radix), and base 1 is tally notation. State is one value plus the row you are editing, which keeps exactly what you typed. Below the rows, the edited number is written out as a sum of digit x base^power.
features: Numbers of any length, exact (BigInt)
Bases 1 (tally) to 36; choose which to show, with the choice remembered
Negative numbers; spaces and underscores ignored when pasting
Place-value breakdown for the base you are editing, e.g. 255 = 2·10² + 5·10¹ + 5·10⁰
Invalid digits named inline while the other rows keep the last good value
Copy button and digit count on each row

title: Color Picker - Sliders
description: RGB, HSV, HSL and OKLCH sliders that paint the colors they would reach, with contrast checks, copyable CSS and saved swatches.
about: Three canvas sliders pick a color in RGB, HSV, HSL or OKLCH. Each track is repainted with the colors that moving only that slider would reach, so the tracks always show the neighborhood of the current color. OKLCH is converted through Björn Ottosson's OKLab matrices; out-of-gamut stretches of a track are drawn as a thin line and the readout flags clipped colors. Contrast against white and black uses the WCAG 2 relative-luminance formula.
features: Four color models (RGB, HSV, HSL, OKLCH), converting between them without losing hue on grays
Out-of-gamut regions shown on OKLCH tracks
Type a hex, rgb() or hsl() color to set the sliders
One-click copy as hex, rgb(), hsl() or oklch()
WCAG contrast ratio and AA/AAA grade against white and black text
Saved swatches kept in localStorage
Keyboard-operable sliders (arrows, Shift for bigger steps, Home/End)

title: Named Color Picker
description: Nearly 5,000 named colors laid out as a slice through color space, with pick-your-own axes, name search and nearest-name lookup.
about: Named colors from the color.pizza API are laid out as a slice through color space. You choose which component (hue, saturation, lightness, value, red, green or blue) goes on the rows, which one sorts each row, and which one the slider filters on, with an adjustable window that wraps around for hue. Type any hex and it finds the nearest named color by distance in OKLab, a space where straight-line distance roughly matches how different two colors look.
features: Choose the component for the rows, the row sort and the slider (picking one already in use swaps them)
Adjustable slider window that wraps around for hue
Search by name, highlighting matches in the grid
Nearest named color for any hex, measured in OKLab, with the distance shown
Copy the selected color's hex
Count of colors currently shown

title: Division Remainder Pattern
description: A zoomable, pannable map of fractions n/d, each pixel shaded by its decimal length, repeating period or remainder.
about: Each pixel is a fraction: the row gives the numerator and the column the denominator. The pixel is shaded by one of three rules: how many characters JavaScript prints for the result (the original pen's rule), the exact length of the repeating decimal, or the remainder n mod d. The period is the multiplicative order of 10 modulo the reduced denominator once its factors of 2 and 5 are removed, cached per denominator. Click a cell to pin it; long division then shows its exact decimal with the repeating block in parentheses.
features: Three shading rules: decimal length, repeating period, remainder
Greyscale or color palette
Zoom from 1/3x to 4x with the wheel or buttons, centered on the cursor
Drag to pan; arrow keys, +/- and 0 also work
Click to pin a cell and see its exact repeating decimal, e.g. 1/7 = 0.(142857)

title: Media List
description: A tag-filtered list of favorite films, games, books and albums with search, sorting, a random pick and shareable filter links.
about: A collection of films, shows, games, books and albums, filtered by tags that narrow each other: each remaining tag shows how many of the visible items carry it, and related tags are joined into segmented groups. Albums open a Bandcamp player and everything else shows the intro of its Wikipedia article, fetched live. Selected tags are mirrored into the URL hash, so a filtered view can be bookmarked or shared.
features: Tags that narrow each other, with live counts and grouped segments
Text search across titles, artists and tags
Sort by artist, year (grouped by decade) or title (grouped by letter)
"Surprise me" opens and scrolls to a random item from the current view
Selected tags kept in the URL hash (#tags=game,ps2) so filtered views can be shared
Inline Bandcamp players and Wikipedia summaries

title: QR Code Generator
description: A QR code generator written from scratch: Reed–Solomon error correction, masking and all, with SVG and PNG export.
about: Type text or a URL and a QR code redraws as you type. The encoder is written from scratch following ISO/IEC 18004. It picks the densest mode, adds Reed–Solomon check bytes over GF(256) and interleaves the blocks, then places the bits in a zigzag around the finder, timing and alignment patterns and keeps the mask with the lowest penalty score. A highlight mode colors the function patterns so you can see which modules carry data.
features: All 40 versions and all four error correction levels (L/M/Q/H)
Automatic numeric, alphanumeric or UTF-8 byte mode
Best of 8 masks chosen by the standard's penalty rules, or force one
Highlight finders, timing, alignment, format and version information
Custom colors, optional quiet zone, SVG and PNG download
Every version tested by decoding the output with jsQR

title: Breathe
description: A paced-breathing guide: a circle swells and shrinks at about six breaths a minute.
about: Slow breathing near six breaths a minute is the best-supported relaxation technique among the games in this set, though the trials are small and varied. This is a pacer, not a measurement: it can't see your heart rate. The animation is computed from the clock rather than accumulated frames, so the circle never drifts if a frame is dropped.
features: 4 to 8 breaths per minute
Even or longer-exhale rhythm
1, 3, 5 or 10 minute sessions
Soft cosine easing at the turnarounds

title: Recall
description: Spaced-repetition flashcards: try to recall first, then check, and cards come back after longer gaps.
about: Retrieval practice and spaced repetition are the best-evidenced techniques in the cognitive-training literature, but they help only for the material you practise. Recall uses a five-box Leitner scheduler with intervals of 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 days. The deck is plain text, one card per line, and editing it keeps progress for cards whose text hasn't changed.
features: Recall before reveal, with an optional typed answer
Missed cards drop back to box 0, due tomorrow
Edit the deck as plain text: front | back
Progress kept in localStorage
Scheduler covered by unit tests

title: Go / No-Go
description: Press for the green circle, hold still for the red square. A mirror for reaction time and impulse control.
about: A classic measure of response inhibition. It's here as a self-measurement, not a workout: training this task hasn't been shown to improve attention in daily life. A block is 60 trials, three in four go, with a random gap so you can't settle into a beat. Reaction times are measured from the frame the stimulus is painted, using a double requestAnimationFrame.
features: Exact 25% no-go share, shuffled
Mean reaction time, variability, misses and slips
Space bar or tap
Best run saved
Trial generation and scoring covered by unit tests

title: Pairs
description: Concentration: find the matching shape-and-color pairs on a 2×2 to 6×6 board.
about: Each pair shares both a shape and a hue, so you can remember it by form, by color or both. There's no clock, only a move count. There's little evidence that matching games improve memory in general, so it's a calm way to pass a few minutes. The deck is shuffled with Fisher-Yates, and a mismatch is held face-up briefly before turning back.
features: No timer, fewest moves wins
Best moves saved per board size

title: Breakout
description: A retro bat-and-ball game with a calm mode: a slower ball and no lives to lose.
about: Nobody has tested whether a game this simple does anything for your brain, so it makes no claim. The rules live in a plain module and are tested without a browser; the component draws the state to a pixelated canvas. Where the ball lands on the paddle sets its angle, and sub-stepping keeps the ball from tunnelling through bricks.
features: Mouse, touch or arrow keys
Calm mode: slower ball, infinite lives
Paddle-angle control
Rules covered by unit tests
